A simple diagram of HIV infection. Left: a round HIV virus particle in cross-section showing the outer envelope with surface proteins, the protein coat (capsid), two strands of RNA and the reverse transcriptase enzyme. Right: a larger CD4 T-helper white blood cell with HIV particles attaching to it, one particle inside, and new HIV particles budding out from its surface. Below, a simple line graph of "CD4 cell count" falling slowly over about ten years, with "HIV in blood" high at first, falling, then rising again, and a shaded section marked "AIDS".

A line graph of antibody concentration in the blood (vertical axis) against time in days (horizontal axis). An arrow at day 0 followed by a small, slow rise and fall in antibody (primary response). A second arrow at a later time followed by a fast, tall and long-lasting rise (secondary response). A dashed horizontal line.
